notes: Union of 3 ranker + 7 inventory drafts (3,132 raw entries -> 1,628 unique -> 1,120 kept). Dedupe key: Devanagari normalized for nukta (फ/फ़), chandrabindu/anusvara, spacing, hyphens and punctuation, plus a hand-built alias map that merged spelling/wording variants (e.g. यह=यह/ये, वह/वो, पैसा->पैसे, रुपया->रुपये, हेलो->हैलो, तबियत->तबीयत, दवा->दवाई, हॉस्पिटल->अस्पताल, खुले पैसे/खुल्ले->छुट्टे, पेट भर गया->बस पेट भर गया, खाना खा लिया?->खाना खाया?, and all duplicate tense/imperative/compound-verb paradigm write-ups). बस kept twice deliberately: bas 'enough' (t1) vs bus the vehicle, shown as बस (वाहन) (t2). Tiers: median of the drafts containing the item, with inventory agents' tiers overriding rankers inside their own domain; .5 medians rounded down. Order: tier, then r1's pedagogical order, then inventory domain order (numbers/time -> family -> food/home -> health -> function words -> verbs -> transport/phone/weather). Counts: t1 217, t2 421, t3 423, t4 59. Over-cap resolution: enumerated-set paradigms redundant with the inventories' individual entries were merged away; all tier-6 and tier-5 items plus single-source tier-4 tail were dropped and are listed verbatim in dropped. Per-item annotation notes from the drafts were pruned for size; the fully annotated build (with per-item merged-variant notes) is at scratchpad/final.json. Learner-profile choices preserved: spoken forms as headwords, assimilated loans (टाइम, थैंक यू, वेज/नॉन-वेज, बीपी, शुगर) ranked as the drafts placed them, in-law/kinship and phone-call chunks retained at high tiers.
adversaryVerdict: This is a strong, genuinely colloquial syllabus: the loan-first register is handled well (टाइम tier 1 with समय marked formal, वेज/टेस्टी, ज़ीरो over शून्य), the kinship and in-law coverage is excellent, and the compound-verb paradigms (कर दो / खा लो, hs-0584/0585) are exactly the spoken backbone most courses miss. The weaknesses are concentrated in four places. First, small-talk domains for precisely this learner are thin: asking after relatives' jobs/studies (नौकरी, पढ़ाई, कॉलेज), evening TV (सीरियल, मैच, न्यूज़), morning/night greetings, phone-availability loans (बिज़ी/फ्री), and hospitality staples (क्या लेंगे?, खाना खाकर जाओ) – hence most of the additions. Second, several tier inversions: words lagging their own chunk or paradigm (ने, छुट्टे, मिल गया) and loan/shuddh pairs tiered backwards (हैप्पी बर्थडे vs जन्मदिन मुबारक, स्वादिष्ट vs टेस्टी). Third, romanisation style drifts that will confuse an SRS learner (dhire/dheere, keejiye/kijiye, accha/achchha, minat/minute, ham/hum, nahi/nahin), plus one outright error: गीज़र as "geezer" (an old man) instead of "geyser". Fourth, housekeeping the schema can't express: hs-0205 (यह क्या है?) duplicates hs-0100 (ये क्या है?) and one should be deleted; hs-0765 (चोट लगी) and hs-0965 (चोट लग गई) are near-duplicates worth merging; साठ romanised "saath" collides exactly with साथ (hs-0136) and सात is "saat" one letter away – consider "saathh" or a disambiguating note; and kahan/kahaan spelling varies across ~10 items and deserves one standard.
dropped: merged redundant paradigms: clock-system; colours; days-of-week; decades; months; numbers 1-10; numbers 11-20 (each covered by individually enumerated entries)
